standard: Answer every requested part against the frozen source-backed key, accepting equivalent wording. A material missing requested fact is partial when the rest is substantially accurate. Do not require unrelated background merely because it appears in a key. Evaluate volunteered contradictions as well as omissions.

Q02.decision: Starting troops includes the troop allocation, not just the initially garrisoned troops. Omitting the other nine troops in supply is a material omission and produces partial, not incorrect.
Q02.reason: The question explicitly asks for starting troops alongside score, Agents and water. The frozen key specifies three garrison troops and nine supply troops. The source calls all twelve cubes troops and separately locates the three in the garrison and the remaining components in supply. Nine reserve troops are part of the requested starting troop state; this is not unasked general component background. An answer need not literally say twelve if it gives three plus nine. The four unused Influence cubes are unasked background and are not required.

Q12.decision: Require the 2-Influence VP and its loss, the 4-Influence track bonus and retention/re-earning, the first-to-4 Alliance and its VP, no theft by tying, and the VP consequences when the Alliance transfers.
Q12.reason: Re-earning after returning to 4 is part of how the requested 4-Influence reward behaves following a reversal. Alliance-VP loss and gain are part of the requested reversibility of the reward at 4. Saying the token passes identifies its ownership change, but does not fully explain what happens to the score: a player could otherwise wrongly keep the original VP as they keep the separate track bonus. These omissions are material under the fixed key. Neither omission makes an otherwise substantial answer wholly incorrect. Specific resource quantities printed on individual Faction tracks are not required because the frozen key accepts 'the track bonus'. FAQ scenarios involving a holder's Influence decrease are additional background beyond the fixed key; their omission is not penalized. The permitted main-rulebook extraction does not independently verify those added FAQ claims, so their presence alone is not classified as an error.
